titulo: AI Jitters and US Midterms Drive Volatility
resumo: November 2026 brought intense cross-currents to global financial markets, dominated by a stunning Democratic sweep in the US midterms and mounting anxiety over the artificial intelligence boom. **Stock markets experienced severe turbulence**, punctuated by a historic $2.5 trillion rout in tech shares following the congressional elections and corporate governance scandals. Meanwhile, **energy prices tumbled significantly** as diplomatic hopes in the Middle East drove Brent crude down. Central bank policy expectations also shifted, with investors grappling with sticky inflation prints and fresh rate-hike murmurs.

sumup.frase: Markets navigated political shifts and **AI jitters** as investors weighed growth against mounting inflation.
sumup.porque: Uncertainty over AI valuations, political gridlock, and hot inflation data kept market participants on edge.

drivers.texto: Democrats flipped control of Congress in the midterms, triggering an initial relief rally before sparking fears of tighter AI regulations and increased fiscal scrutiny. The S&P 500 closed at 7549.94 on November 9, down 0.4% for the month.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.7% on the month, settling at 25253.14 on November 9, as investors reacted to soaring infrastructure costs and corporate governance concerns. Equity volatility spiked, with the VIX rising 2.6% over the month to 19.92.

Brent crude tumbled 10.9% during the month to 107.03 USD a barrel on November 3, driven by easing tensions and hopes for peace talks regarding Iran. Lower oil prices offered some relief to headline inflation concerns globally.

drivers.factor: Hot Inflation and Rate Hike Fears
drivers.texto: Hotter-than-expected inflation reports rekindled market anxiety over potential monetary tightening by central banks. US Treasury 10-year yields ended down 6bp at 4.88%, while 2-year yields held flat at 4.56%.

themes.texto: The artificial intelligence sector faced a reality check as massive capital expenditure requirements collided with political pushback and data center moratoriums. Despite soaring revenue announcements from firms like Anthropic and massive consolidation moves such as Marvell's acquisition announcements, investors grew increasingly nervous about profitability timelines. Cybersecurity incidents, memory chip shortages, and high borrowing costs for neocloud providers highlighted the underlying credit and execution risks in the AI supply chain.

Persistent inflation readings across major economies forced markets to re-evaluate the trajectory of monetary easing. With Euro area inflation remaining at 4% in October 2026 and Portugal's inflation at 3.9%, policymakers faced continued challenges. Although the ECB deposit rate remained at 2.5%, hotter data in the US provoked renewed debate over whether further rate hikes might be required to tame stubborn price pressures.

Market sentiment was further tested by high-profile corporate investigations and security breaches. Nvidia's stock faced intense pressure following reports concerning an internal investigation into its CEO, adding to general jitters after a massive $6.3 billion crypto heist at Binance. These events underscored the vulnerability of high-valuation tech and crypto ecosystems to operational and leadership risks.

questoes.q: Will the Democratic congressional sweep lead to aggressive federal regulations on AI?
questoes.porque: New legislative control could introduce strict oversight, data center moratoria, and compliance costs that threaten tech profit margins.
questoes.sinais: Introduction of specific bipartisan tech restriction bills or official policy announcements from newly empowered committee leaders.

questoes.q: Are central banks finished raising interest rates or is a new hiking cycle beginning?
questoes.porque: Hotter inflation prints have revived fears that borrowing costs will remain restrictive for longer or even increase further.
questoes.sinais: Upcoming consumer price index releases and official remarks from Federal Reserve and ECB policymakers.

questoes.q: Can massive AI infrastructure investments generate enough revenue to justify current valuations?
questoes.porque: Soaring capital expenditures and high-yield debt issuance by AI-adjacent companies have raised concerns over potential credit strain.
questoes.sinais: Quarterly earnings reports and cloud computing revenue growth metrics from major hyperscalers.

momentos.facto: Marvell announced a massive deal involving Lumentum while oil prices slid on US-Iran diplomatic hopes.
US voters went to the polls for midterm elections as tech stocks attempted to steady after recent sessions of volatility.
US stocks rallied significantly as Democrats swept control of Congress, sending the Dow to a strong one-day relief gain.
A historic tech sell-off wiped out trillions from the Nasdaq as investors feared imminent AI regulation and spending limits.
Global equities attempted a tentative rebound following a stronger-than-expected US monthly jobs report showing 165,000 jobs added in October.
Nvidia shares tumbled after the company opened an investigation into its chief executive officer, increasing governance jitters.
Hotter-than-expected inflation data sparked renewed bond market selling and pushed Treasury yields higher on rate-hike worries.

classes.leitura: Major indices traded lower over the month amid intense tech volatility, though cushioned by post-midterm relief bounces.
Treasury yields experienced modest movement, with 10-year yields dropping 6bp while rate-hike anxieties lingered.
Oil prices retreated sharply by double digits due to easing Middle East tensions and diplomatic de-escalation hopes.
European markets posted gains supported by banking and technology advances alongside easing regional energy pressures.
US high-yield credit spreads tightened slightly by 10bp over the month, remaining resilient despite equity turbulence.
The EUR/USD exchange rate ticked up 0.4% over the month to 1.1214 on November 10.
